subject: Follow-up: SDK routing, streaming semantics & chat vs completions questions
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Sara Park <sara@octavehealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: SDK routing, streaming semantics & chat vs completions questions

Thanks again for the call today — good first pass. Below is a short recap and a few technical items we promised to follow up on so your engineers have the detail they need for a POC.

Recap (high level):
- Goal: replace current in-house reranker + prompt orchestration with a single Redwood-backed endpoint that handles chat orchestration, embeddings-based rerank, and a small tool-calling hook for PHI-safe lookup (redacted tokens, no raw PHI stored in logs).
- Preferred deployment: Redwood Hosted for initial POC, then Dedicated or Private depending on compliance.
- Success metrics: sub-200ms median token latency for chat streaming + top-5 MRR for reranker on sample queries.

Action items / technical questions (please see numbered items for your engineers):
1) SDK & auth: do you prefer API-key per service account (short-lived) or OAuth service principal? For the POC we can support either; we recommend API-key + mTLS when using Dedicated/Private.
2) Routing: you asked about routing different request types (embeddings vs chat vs rerank). We recommend a single logical API with model routing rules (route by route-type + intent header). Do you want a split endpoint per capability or a unified endpoint?
3) Structured output / tool calling: proposal is to use our function-calling style (json-schema contract) for the PHI lookup call; we can validate against your schema at the edge and reject malformed requests. Will your lookup be sync (RPC) or async?
4) Embeddings & reranking: how many candidates do you plan to score (top-k from vector DB)? Typical POCs use k=100 then rerank top 10 with the model. Any constraints on batch sizes from your vector store?
5) Chat vs completions semantics: important for integration — streaming delta tokens and stop sequences behavior differ across endpoints. Do you need a deterministic stop (hard stop token) or streaming early-exit heuristics?
6) Tokenization / max_tokens: what is your typical doc length and prompt headroom? We'll recommend token budget and suggest dynamic truncation/bucketed contexts.

Attachments: I attached a short integration checklist and a permissive sample schema that demonstrates function calling + structured outputs. See attached: redwood-mpam-integration-checklist.pdf, sample-schema.json

Next steps:
- Share answers to items 1–6 (your devs can reply inline)
- We propose a 90-min POC kickoff on Mon 11/16 or Tue 11/17 to run through SDK auth, a demo of streaming, and a live rerank test.

Thanks — happy to jump on a follow-up with your engineering leads.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0142

Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 16:05:12 -0500
Subject: Re: Follow-up: SDK routing, streaming semantics & chat vs completions questions

Thanks Marcus — appreciate the clear list. Quick answers from our side (engineering copy + follow-ups):

1) Auth: for the POC we'll start with API keys scoped to the POC project. For production we need token rotation with our IAM (OAuth/OIDC). We also want request-level auditing headers (X-Request-Id) that show up in logs.
2) Routing: prefer a unified endpoint with a route-type header (X-Redwood-Op: chat|embed|rerank). Simpler for our gateway.
3) Tool calling: lookup will be sync for now (fast RPC). We'll want to ensure we can redact returned values before they get persisted; ideally Redwood can call a transform webhook before any logs are written. Any existing hooks for that?
4) Embeddings: we'll return ~200 candidates from our vector DB and expect Redwood to score top-20. Vector DB (Pinecone) supports batch scoring; we can limit to batches of 50.
5) Stop tokens: we need deterministic hard stops for certain content pipes (e.g., consent paragraphs). We'll want explicit stop-token handling; streaming is okay but must respect stop sequences and close the stream on hard stop.
6) Docs: average input doc is 6k chars; prompt headroom desired = 2k tokens.

We can confirm POC kickoff Tue 11/17 09:00 PT. I'll loop in our engineering lead if you want deeper API-level calls.

— Sara
Sara Park
Head of Product, Integrations | Octave Health
sara@octavehealth.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Sara Park <sara@octavehealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 09:08:22 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: SDK routing, streaming semantics & chat vs completions questions

Appreciate the quick answers — a few clarifications and platform recommendations from our infra side so your engineers can design against them: 

A) Auth + auditing: we support API keys with rotation and can inject request-id into logs. For OAuth/OIDC we can federate to your IAM (we use short-lived tokens internally). For Dedicated/Private we also support mTLS.
B) Unified endpoint + routing header: aligns with our recommended pattern. We will expose route hints (X-Redwood-Op) and a model selector header. That allows your gateway to keep a single upstream.
C) Tool-calling / pre-log transform: we have a transform-hook feature on Private/Dedicated that lets you run a filter before logs are persisted; for hosted we can redact fields at ingestion (configurable). We'll attach a short checklist with options.
D) Batch sizing: we'll accept batches of up to 64 for scoring and will shard internally for higher counts; scoring top-20 is trivial. For Pinecone we recommend k=200 fetch then incremental scoring windows of 50.
E) Stops & streaming behavior: important notes —
   - Chat streaming: we stream deltas as they are generated. Hard stop sequences are enforced server-side and will trigger immediate stream termination.
   - Completions endpoint: non-chat completions will return the whole completion object when done and honor stop tokens; streaming is available but semantics differ (no role-based messages).
   - Recommendation: use chat endpoint for interactive UX and streaming, completions for short single-shot generation where you don't need message history.
F) Token budget: given 2k token headroom and "6k chars" average, recommend a 4k token model for POC and dynamic truncation on history.

I'm attaching the checklist and a sample schema that demonstrates the function-calling contract we'll use for the lookup RPC.

— Marcus

Attachments: redwood-mpam-integration-checklist.pdf, sample-schema.json

Small note from prompt engineering / tokenization perspective:
- "6k chars" ~= ~1100 tokens (depending on language). With requested headroom of 2k tokens, your end-to-end context fits comfortably in a 4k-token model, but if you plan to add more system/history we should consider a 8k model.
- Stop sequences: if you have structured outputs (function-calling JSON) use explicit end-of-structure tokens and validate on the client so partial streams don't cause parse errors.
- For rerank prompts: prefer normalized candidate concatenation and a separator token to ensure consistent token counts during scoring.

— Lauren
Principal Prompt Engineer | Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2026 10:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: SDK routing, streaming semantics & chat vs completions questions

Quick infra note before kickoff on Tue:
- Streaming implementation: for chat streaming we expose chunked SSE (server-sent events) and websocket options. Each chunk contains 'delta' tokens and a final 'done' event. We provide SDK helpers that reassemble tokens and guard against partial JSON function-calls (they buffer until the full JSON payload is observed).
- If you need strict byte-level determinism for stop tokens, use the non-streaming completions path for final deterministic outputs. For user-facing interactivity use chat streaming + client-side parse-safe buffering.
- KV cache implication: if your reranker uses cached contexts we can pin session keys to speed up warm calls; let us know if you want session affinity in the POC.

See you all tomorrow at 9:00 PT — I'll share a short agenda and a link to the demo env.

— Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
